key_insight: PRISM shows that a small number of real human interaction videos can be amplified into a much larger and more diverse training set using counterfactual video generation. This makes it possible to scale humanoid loco-manipulation learning without needing massive amounts of expensive real-world video data.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the data bottleneck in teaching humanoids loco-manipulation skills through visual imitation. High-quality videos of full-body, unoccluded human-object interactions are hard to collect at scale, limiting the diversity and robustness of learned behaviors.
method: Uses a real-to-sim-to-real framework to convert a few real demonstrations into scalable training data.
Generates counterfactual videos to create diverse, plausible variations of human-object interactions from limited source clips.
Trains humanoid control policies from the expanded video set so the robot can learn broader carrying and manipulation behaviors.
impact: This approach lowers the cost and labor required to train humanoid robots from visual demonstrations, making generalist loco-manipulation more practical. For practitioners, it offers a scalable path to improve robot skill diversity without relying on large curated video datasets.
